PullRequest.Title: Add Back navigation to plugin marketplace quick picks
PullRequest.Body:

Marketplace management pages did not provide a way to return to the marketplace list, forcing users to cancel and reopen the command. The Add Plugin Marketplace input and marketplace action picker now use the existing Back QuickInputButton to return directly to their parent list.

- Adds Back navigation to local and provider-backed marketplace action pickers.
- Adds Back navigation to the Add Plugin Marketplace input.
- Preserves existing Escape, validation, add, and remove behavior.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — Passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — Passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\actions\chatPluginActions.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\actions\chatPluginActions.test.ts` — Passed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\actions\chatPluginActions.test.ts` — Passed with 26 tests.
- Live Code OSS validation — Both Back buttons returned to the marketplace list; the button exposed `Back (Alt+LeftArrow)` and rendered with the Codicon font.

Scenarios.Scenario: Manage locally configured plugin marketplaces and return from an existing marketplace action picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration reads and parsing build the parent list; selecting a marketplace awaits one filesystem existence check before the child action picker appears. Pressing Back rebuilds the parent list immediately, but does not repeat the filesystem check unless the user selects a marketplace again.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check whether the selected marketplace repository directory exists to decide whether to show Open Folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One check per marketplace selection; zero merely from pressing Back until another marketplace is selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same existence check ran before the action picker prior to the PR. Returning via cancel and reopening/reselecting also incurred one check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks display of the marketplace action picker for the selected local marketplace.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective configured marketplace count after canonical-ID deduplication; list construction and policy checks are linear in that count. Filesystem checks occur only for the single selected marketplace.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized by the action's while loop and awaited quick inputs; at most one filesystem existence check is outstanding.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration is reread on each parent-list display so mutations are reflected. Repository URI lookup may use the service's in-memory marketplace index; file existence itself is not cached here. Cold and warm behavior have the same one-check cardinality for a selected marketplace.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed loop, unchanged fileService.exists call, and direct call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository filesystem latency varies by URI/provider, but the diff does not increase effective check cardinality for an equivalent return-and-reselect workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: Back adds bounded parent-list reconstruction, while the expensive filesystem boundary remains one per explicit marketplace selection and was already present.

Scenarios.Scenario: Manage provider-backed marketplaces and return from add/action child inputs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each parent-list display awaits provider.list before showing inventory. The concrete agent-host provider delegates this to IAgentHostService.listPluginMarketplaces, which crosses the agent-host management boundary and ultimately calls the Copilot SDK marketplace-list RPC. Back re-enters the serialized loop and waits for one fresh inventory call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List plugin marketplaces through the agent-host service and provider SDK RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call on initial command display and one additional call for each explicit Back return to the parent list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no in-command Back path; the equivalent user workflow required cancelling and reopening the command, which also issued one provider.list call. The PR does not increase boundary cardinality for returning to the inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The parent marketplace picker cannot reappear until inventory returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Add, refresh, or remove a provider marketplace through agent-host management.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per accepted add or refresh; remove may make a second forced call after explicit confirmation. Back makes none of these mutation calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These provider mutation calls and their cardinality predate the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Mutations block progression as before; they are not executed on Back.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One inventory RPC per parent-list display; returned item mapping is linear in provider marketplace count. Effective cardinality is one RPC, not one per marketplace.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized: provider.list completes before the picker is shown, and each Back iteration begins only after the child input resolves. No burst or overlapping list calls is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: This action does not cache provider inventory; each display asks the authoritative provider. Any lower-layer SDK caching is unspecified. Back therefore has the same cold/warm boundary shape: one call, with duration dependent on provider/agent-host state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the provider implementation delegating directly to listPluginMarketplaces and the test asserting exactly two list calls across initial display plus one Back.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent-host and SDK RPC latency varies, especially for remote-backed sessions, but only one serialized inventory call occurs per explicit parent return.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: although direct Back performs one authoritative inventory RPC, it replaces the prior cancel-and-reopen path with the same one-call cost, with no fan-out or concurrency amplification.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type, validate, accept, cancel, or go Back from Add Plugin Marketplace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Typing now performs synchronous reference parsing plus a linear duplicate scan and updates quick-input validation state. Back hides and disposes the input without filesystem, network, or provider mutation work. Acceptance performs the same configuration update or provider add boundary as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Add a marketplace through the provider after valid acceptance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per accepted provider source; zero on Back or invalid acceptance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider add already occurred once after accepted input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks returning to the refreshed provider inventory after acceptance.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the local marketplace configuration after valid acceptance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One update per accepted local source; zero on Back or invalid input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single configuration update occurred after accepted input.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Validation cost scales with keystroke count times configured marketplace count; configured sources are parsed once before typing, and each keystroke parses only the current input then scans canonical IDs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Validation is synchronous on the UI event path with no asynchronous overlap. Add/configuration updates remain one serialized operation after acceptance.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Parsed configured references are retained for the lifetime of one input. There is no cross-input cache; reopening reparses configured sources. No negative-cache behavior applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that validation moved from the quick-input controller's 100 ms debounce to every value-change event, but also high confidence that the work has no expensive boundary and reuses pre-parsed configured references.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users can configure arbitrary marketplace counts, but typical inventories are small and validation consists of bounded string parsing plus an in-memory scan; no evidence establishes realistic jank.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the per-keystroke work is lightweight and bounded for realistic marketplace inventories, while Back avoids all mutation boundaries and disposes the input lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose a marketplace action using the new custom QuickPick
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The custom picker allocates one QuickPick and DisposableStore, renders a small fixed action list, and resolves on accept, Back, or hide. Hiding synchronously triggers lifecycle cleanup through onDidHide and store.dispose.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Action item count is fixed and very small: local marketplaces expose at most three actions and provider marketplaces at most two.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One picker is active at a time; completion is guarded and the enclosing workflow remains serialized.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Picker state exists only for one child interaction and is disposed on hide.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the helper's complete/hide/onDidHide flow and QuickInput lifecycle implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Quick-input rendering duration is not measured, but cardinality is fixed and the custom implementation performs no new external operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: allocation and rendering are bounded, and cleanup runs on every completion path.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced local and provider-backed marketplace list, add, action, validation, and Back workflows. The only expensive changed-path boundary is one authoritative provider inventory IPC on direct Back; it is serialized and matches the prior cancel/reopen workflow rather than amplifying work. Custom quick inputs have bounded item counts and dispose on hide; synchronous validation is lightweight with no expensive boundary. No actionable performance regression was found.
